1.why: Verify-token requires record.sessionId === session.id and a matching accountBinding before accepting the reset token.

2.why: A token from another session fails the sessionId check, so the same reset code does not work for any other user.

3.why: Password reset only mutates the current session; no other entries in the sessions Map are invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS and non-https requests are rejected, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256 digests and passwords bcrypt-hashed; that is hashing/protection, not encryption of user data.

6.why: There is no real email; API copy is generic and does not echo private contact fields, though mock tokens are returned locally.

7.why: requestJson caps body size; contact, token, password, and MFA inputs are type/length/charset validated before use.

8.why: The app performs no redirects and only serves fixed same-origin paths, rejecting query strings and hashes.

9.why: There are no email templates; mock delivery logs server-generated tokens without inserting user-controlled HTML.

10.why: recoveryToken and mfaCode are returned in API JSON and written to the on-page Logs panel and console.

11.why: Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded value "482916" in source.

12.why: No default username/password pair exists, yet the MFA confirmation code is always the fixed default 482916.

13.why: Recovery, token verification, and MFA endpoints rate-limit and lock out after repeated failed attempts.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same generic message whether or not the contact is recognized.

15.why: Tokens are 32-byte crypto-random values bound to the requesting session, though accountBinding is a constant opaque string.
